newsitem.title: UK: NWE heating oil cargoes steady on French strike.
newsitem.headline: NWE heating oil cargoes steady on French strike.

text.p: A French oil workers' strike continued to support NWE gas oil cargo premiums on Wednesday against downward pressure from low demand and good supply in the Rotterdam barge market, traders said.

Dec IPE futures were unchanged at $222.75 a tonne in thin volumes but heating oil cargoes were firm at Dec IPE +$6.50/7.50 cif NWE with the stoppage continuing to shut in up to a quarter of French refining capacity.
Russian was seen steady at Dec IPE +$4/5 while low sulphur diesel was around Dec IPE +17/18.
Volume as very low in both cargo and barge markets. Mild German weather was a major curb on demand, traders said.

"The end-user argues 'Why do I have to buy today when I can pick up cheaper in two months' time'. There is also an end-of-year feeling making some of us want to leave the market alone and not risk our 1997 performance figures," a barge trader said.
Another trader said: "We are at a level that everybody is satisfied with. But nobody knows where to go from here."
Bulls said plans by AIC, the main short on the disputed IPE Nov expiry, to sell 160,000-190,000 tonnes of gas oil into ARA was factored into the price and was not now a major factor.
